api_reference.example_scope: MS86 model/workflow usage with every assertion removed. This is API usage, not a ready partial-invoicing implementation.

instruction: Return one structured replacement edit for the exact placeholder // LIGHTYEAR_BUILDER_JOURNEY\n in LightyearOperationsTest.java. Do not use tools. Generate a new operations Java JUnit test in org.idempiere.test extending AbstractTestCase, using the pinned real model/workflow APIs. Do not hard-code predicted business results or substitute SQL writes for application workflows. Read observed totals and flags from saved objects. Independent private gates judge the committed native database. You cannot change those gates. After any failure, only the attached analyst diagnostic objects may inform a repair. Preserve the initial scenario and trace contract. The edit always replaces the placeholder with the complete candidate, including on repair.
journey: Create a customer/location, stocked product/price, opening inventory and order. Complete two shipments for quantities 1 then 2, followed by ONE aggregate invoice for quantity 3 and payment of its observed grand total. Post invoice, payment and allocations using the application APIs without reposting already-posted documents. Create a quantity-1 credit memo against that invoice, complete and post it, then Reverse_Correct it through the workflow and read the reversal and accounting. Inject an exception after saving a draft customer in a separate transaction; explicitly roll it back, retry once with logical key LY-BOUNDARY-RETRY, then repeat lookup to prove caller-keyed idempotency. With two overlapping transactions, use Query.setForUpdate(true).list() on exactly one customer primary key, increment the credit limit by 0.01 in each, coordinate with latches and record the lock wait and readbacks. Use application models/workflows for business writes, never SQL substitutes. Independently captured final rows and the frozen private judge determine the outcome.
